title: Fraction Computation: One Rule per Operation
preview: Anchor on same-denominator addition, then move through different denoms, subtraction, multiplication (new rule!), and division. Pairs with the Fluency drills.

body.goal: Students articulate the four fraction-operation rules — common denominator for ±, multiply across for ×, multiply by the reciprocal for ÷ — by walking through carefully varied cases.
body.launch: Open with the prerequisite warm-up so they're solid on equivalent fractions. Then run the slice. Don't pre-teach the rules. After the slice, the Fluency Practice button on this section gives individual drill reps.
body.prerequisiteLabel: Warm up: equivalent fractions and reciprocals.

steps.teacherNote: Anchor — same denominator. Add numerators only.
Different denominators. Push: 'find a common denominator first.'
One denominator is a multiple of the other — only one fraction needs rewriting.
No shared factor — LCD is the product.
Switch to subtraction. Same common-denominator rule. Simplify the answer.
Switch to multiplication. NEW rule: multiply numerators and multiply denominators. No common denominator needed!
Same rule. Simplify at the end.
Switch to division. NEW rule: multiply by the reciprocal. 1/2 × 4/1 = 4/2 = 2.

enrichmentSteps.teacherNote: Mixed number — convert to improper first.

body.consolidation: Bring the class back. Ask: 'When do you need a common denominator? When DON'T you?' Push: 'Common denominator for + and −; NOT needed for × and ÷.' Then: 'What's the trick that turns ÷ into ×?' Reciprocal. Then point them at the Fluency Practice button — same skill, individual reps.
